division_name: The Adventure Of The Copper Beeches

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.note: Consulting detective of Baker Street, narrator Watson's friend; sharp, abstracted, smokes a long cherry-wood pipe; present throughout the case.

characters.name: Dr. Watson
characters.note: Narrator and Holmes's companion, a medical man who accompanies him to Hampshire and carries a pistol; present throughout.

characters.name: Violet Hunter
characters.note: Young governess with a bright quick freckled face and chestnut hair she cut off; the client who consults Holmes, then is taken to Copper Beeches under a false identity.

characters.name: Jephro Rucastle
characters.note: Stout, smiling, bluff father of Alice Rucastle and husband of the second wife; keeps his daughter imprisoned, sets his mastiff loose, and is mauled by it at the end.

characters.name: Mrs. Rucastle
characters.note: Pale, silent, much younger second wife of Jephro Rucastle; devoted to her husband and son, sad-eyed; not mad.

characters.name: Edward
characters.note: Six-year-old spoiled son of the Rucastles, cruel to weaker creatures; Violet's charge.

characters.name: Alice Rucastle
characters.note: Daughter of Jephro Rucastle by his first wife, heiress with rights of her own by will; supposedly in Philadelphia, actually locked in the barricaded room; not present on stage.

characters.name: Toller
characters.note: Rough, drunken groom and manservant of Copper Beeches, husband of Mrs. Toller; lets the mastiff loose at night.

characters.name: Mrs. Toller
characters.note: Tall, gaunt, sour-faced wife of Toller; cook and servant at Copper Beeches, later locked in the cellar and reveals the plot.

characters.name: Mr. Fowler
characters.note: Alice Rucastle's fiancé, a bearded man in a grey suit who watches the house from the Southampton road, bribed Toller and Mrs. Toller; not present on stage.

characters.name: Miss Stoper
characters.note: Manageress of Westaway's governess agency in the West End who handles Violet's application.

characters.name: Carlo
characters.note: Giant tawny mastiff kept at Copper Beeches, loosed at night and shot by Watson after mauling Rucastle.

locations.name: Baker Street
aliases: the old room at Baker Street
locations.note: Holmes and Watson's sitting-room in London, where Violet Hunter first consults Holmes.

locations.name: Westaway's agency
locations.note: Governess agency in the West End where Violet was offered the post by Rucastle.

locations.name: Black Swan Hotel
locations.note: Inn in the High Street at Winchester where Holmes and Watson meet Violet.

locations.name: Copper Beeches
locations.note: Large whitewashed square house five miles from Winchester in Hampshire, named for its copper beech trees, with a barricaded wing and a dog kennel outbuilding.

locations.name: the barricaded room
locations.note: Locked room in the deserted wing of Copper Beeches, lit by a skylight, where Alice Rucastle was held.

locations.name: the drawing-room
locations.note: Large room along the front of Copper Beeches with three long windows, where Violet sat for the mirror-game and where Rucastle was later laid.

locations.name: the Southampton road
locations.note: Public highway in front of Copper Beeches where Fowler watched from the railings.

brief.tone: Quiet, foggy domestic unease in London giving way to a sunny but menacing Hampshire countryside, ending in a sudden violent climax; restrained Victorian detective mood rather than gothic excess.
depiction_rules: Show the mastiff's attack only at the end, and keep Rucastle's wounds offstage or lightly suggested rather than graphic.
Do not depict Alice Rucastle's imprisonment in detail; the barricaded room may be shown empty or dim with the bed and linen.
Violet's cut hair may be shown as short and the electric-blue dress as worn but well-fitted.
Holmes is shown in his Baker Street manner with pipe and dressing-gown contexts as appropriate; avoid anachronistic gadgets.
Show the copper beeches as a dark-leafed group of trees before a whitewashed house.

era.name: Late Victorian England, c. 1890s, Hampshire countryside and London
era.people: English middle and working classes: a governess, a stout gentleman, a drunken groom and his wife, a sad young wife and a spoiled child.
era.dress: Victorian day wear: governess's plain neat dress, a cloak and hat, a gentleman's suit with a waistcoat, Violet's electric-blue dress of beige-toned material, working-class servants' plain clothing.
era.buildings_and_objects: Baker Street sitting-room with gas lighting and a coal fire; a whitewashed country house with a drawing-room and long windows; outbuildings and an iron bed used as a barricade; old inns and a cathedral town of Winchester.
era.technology: Telegraph and telegrams, railway trains with timetables (Bradshaw), gas lamps, dog-carts and traps; no motor cars, no telephones at the house, no electric lighting.
